text:
maria: Heads-up — canary rollout r3421 is showing a regression on quantized workloads. p95 token latency up ~30% for our int8 profile and throughput down ~18% on long-context tests. Seen on two clusters in us-west.
sam: ugh. seen similar in perf dashboard. any obvious errors in logs?

maria: no exceptions, just higher CPU on dequant hotloop. KV cache hit rate also dropped ~12%. linking flamegraphs: https://perf.internal/redwood/flames/1976543210 (can view)

lucas: I pulled a trace. The kernel selector is choosing the new "fallback-dequant" path for ~60% of attention layers where previously it went to fast-int8-kernel. Looks like the selector heuristic changed in r3421 to prefer conservative memory bounds for mixed-size blocks.

anya: perf-ci-bot reported a regression in the nightly perf job for the same commit range. attaching CI summary: 
```
perf-ci-bot: nightly/perf-int8: p95 +28%, avg tokens/sec -15%
regression first seen at commit 3f8a9 -> PR #3421 (kernel-selector heuristics)
```

sam: can we bisect to the exact offending commit? I'll start a local bisect on the stable branch.

sam: `git bisect start --term-old=good --term-new=bad 3f8a9 HEAD`

lucas: I ran a quicker bisection on canary images. Bad at 3f8a9e8 -> good at 3f6b2c1. The change is the heuristic around `max_block_memory` and the fallback threshold. Patch moved the threshold from 0.8 -> 0.6 which increases fallback.

maria: that matches the KV numbers — more fallback => different memory access pattern => less reuse of KV caches (evictions earlier). We see `kv_cache_hit` fall in the same time window.

anya: logs: 
```
[2026-03-10T09:12:45Z] kernel_selector: chosen_path=fallback-dequant reason=mem_margin(0.55)<0.6
[2026-03-10T09:12:45Z] kv_cache: hit_rate=0.68 -> was 0.80
```

sam: quick mitigation options: 1) revert heuristic change, 2) ship a rollout flag to force `prefer_fast_int8=true` for canaries, 3) tune KV cache sizing temporarily. Revert seems safest.

lucas: before revert, can we try toggling the selector via config? It can be toggled per-deployment without code rollback. I tested locally by setting `selector.mem_margin_threshold=0.75` and perf returned to baseline in my microbenchmarks.

maria: ok let's flip the flag on the affected canaries and monitor. @deploy-bot can you push `selector.mem_margin_threshold=0.75` to canary group 3?

deploy-bot: rolling config change to canary group 3: `selector.mem_margin_threshold=0.75` (starts)
deploy-bot: update applied to 6/6 nodes in group 3. Monitoring.

maria: after the change p95 is back within 5% of baseline, KV hit rate recovered to 0.79. Preliminary looks good. :thumbsup:

anya: CI-side, we should add a perf test that exercises long-context int8 + mixed precision to catch this before rollout. I'll open a ticket.

sam: file for revert PR anyway with notes from bisect, but we'll hold if config fix is stable. PR draft: `revert: kernel-selector heuristic change (r3421)`

lucas: put a guard in selector to avoid switching to fallback if cache hit_rate over last minute > 0.7 — that should prevent oscillation across mixed workloads. I'll prototype.

maria: action items: 
- anya: add long-context int8 perf test to nightly (P0)
- lucas: prototype guard and push RFC (P1)
- sam: prepare revert PR but don't merge unless config flip fails (P1)
- deploy-bot/perf team: continue monitoring canary for 24h (P0)

maria: thanks everyone. saved a rollback and avoided customer impact for now. We'll follow up with perf numbers in #eng-runtime tomorrow.
